name: Hermes Kanban: The Idempotent Nightly Review
description: A task that files itself onto the board every night and never double-books.

name: Hermes Kanban: The Research-to-Draft Relay
description: Two researchers work in parallel, then a writer's card unblocks once both finish.

name: Hermes Kanban: The Swarm
description: Fan a goal out to N parallel workers, gate a verifier on all of them, then a synthesizer on the verifier.

name: Hermes MoA: stack frontier models into one virtual model for hard turns
description: Configure a Mixture-of-Agents preset in Hermes so several models answer in parallel and an aggregator writes the final response, and validate the preset before you spend double the tokens on it.

name: Hermes on MiMo-V2.5: a 1M-context agent for pennies
description: Set MiMo-V2.5 as your everyday Hermes model: 1M context at $0.14/$0.28 per 1M tokens, with tool-use enforcement on for a non-GPT model.

name: Hermes: a scheduled agentic briefing on Hy3-preview
description: Schedule a hands-off tool-using job (search, summarize, deliver) on the cheap, agentic Hy3-preview model, validated cron + config.

name: Hermes: offload background jobs to MiMo-V2-Flash and cut your main bill
description: Route Hermes' cheap, high-volume auxiliary work (compression, vision, web-extract) to MiMo-V2-Flash so your expensive main model only handles real reasoning.

name: Idea Cross-Pollinator: Find the Links You'd Never Spot
description: Have Claude search your whole vault and surface non-obvious connections to an idea.

name: Khoj + Fable 5: A Second Brain That Knows Your Notes
description: Point a self-hosted assistant at your documents so Fable 5 can answer from your own notes, not just the internet.

name: Kilo Code: a mode that can only edit the files you let it
description: Build a docs mode that can read the whole repo but only write to Markdown, using a fileRegex restriction on the edit group.

name: Kilo Code: add an MCP tool and bind it to one mode
description: Enable an MCP server's tools only on the mode that needs it (a researcher), so its tool definitions don't load into every conversation and burn tokens.

name: Kilo Code: ship a big feature as isolated subtasks with Orchestrator
description: Define the orchestrator's delegate modes (architect, code, debug) so a large task runs as isolated subtasks, each in its own clean context.

name: Let a free model triage your reading: one-line summary + reply flag
description: Point any OpenAI-compatible tool at an OpenRouter free model so each email/article/report comes back as a one-sentence summary plus a needs-reply flag, and you only open what earns it.

name: Letta + Fable 5: Persistent Memory for Multi-Week Projects
description: Give Fable 5 a memory that survives restarts via Letta's structured memory blocks, so a project runs for weeks, not one session.

name: Letta: An Agent That Manages Its Own Memory
description: Install the Letta CLI and SDK, the MemGPT lineage where the agent edits its own memory blocks like an OS pages memory.

name: LibreChat + Fable 5: Show It a Screenshot or a PDF
description: Run a private, self-hosted ChatGPT-style app where you drop in an image or document and let Claude Fable 5 read it.

name: LlamaIndex: index your documents and query them at runtime
description: Point LlamaIndex at a document corpus and build a VectorStoreIndex so an agent can retrieve the relevant chunks at query time instead of stuffing everything into context.

name: Local model chore: draft a sensitive message in private
description: Ask a free, offline model to draft or soften a delicate message (a note about money, a reply to a doctor, a careful complaint) knowing the contents stay on your machine.

name: Local model chore: read a photo with a vision model, on-device
description: Snap a receipt, a medication label, or a handwritten note, and have a free offline vision model read out the details so you do not have to squint and retype.

name: Local model chore: summarize a long PDF without it leaving your laptop
description: Attach a 30-page PDF or a dense terms-of-service to a local model and get five plain bullets plus anything you need to act on, with the document staying on your machine.

name: Local model chore: turn a brain-dump into a clean to-do list
description: Paste messy meeting notes into a free, offline model on your own laptop and get back an organized to-do list, with nothing leaving the machine.

name: Mastra: stop on incomplete private soccer moneyline outcome sets
description: Run a deterministic two-step Mastra workflow that checks supplied soccer moneyline response shapes for one home, away, and Draw outcome before any downstream private analysis, without treating runtime success as data completeness or a betting recommendation.

name: Meeting Processor: Raw Dump to Structured Note
description: Paste a raw meeting dump into your vault and have Claude turn it into action items, decisions, and links.

name: Mem0: A Personalization Layer Your Assistant Remembers With
description: Add user, session, and agent-level memory to an assistant so it remembers preferences across conversations.

name: Mnemosyne: Fully Local Agent Memory, No Cloud at All
description: Give your agent persistent memory in a single SQLite file: store a fact, recall it by keyword, fully offline.

name: Morning Synthesis: a Start-of-Day Note Before Coffee
description: Schedule Claude Code to read your recent notes and write a daily start-of-day briefing.

name: n8n as an MCP server: prove each exposed workflow is one narrow tool behind its own token
description: Expose n8n workflows to an agent through MCP Server Triggers without handing it your whole toolbox, by proving each agent-callable trigger is one narrow workflow behind its own bearer token with no wildcard-HTTP or delete-capable node, so a leaked token or a prompt injection is b

name: Obsidian × MCPVault: Read a Note from Any MCP Client
description: Read a note from your Obsidian vault through MCPVault, from any MCP client, including a fully local LM Studio + open-model setup.

name: Obsidian × MCPVault: The Argument Builder
description: Give Claude a thesis and have it assemble a sourced, ranked argument from everything you've ever written.

name: Obsidian × MCPVault: The Book Notes System
description: Dump your highlights and have Claude file the book into your second brain with connections and project-tied takeaways.

name: Obsidian × MCPVault: The Decision Journal
description: Log decisions with frontmatter, let Claude update the outcome safely, and read the patterns each quarter.

name: Obsidian × MCPVault: The Project Kickoff Generator
description: Hand Claude your goals and constraints and have it scaffold a whole project folder from what your vault already knows.

name: Obsidian × MCPVault: The Vault Health Check
description: A monthly, scheduled audit that finds orphan notes, stale info, and inconsistent tags before your vault rots.

name: Obsidian × MCPVault: Write a Note from Any MCP Client
description: Create or patch a note in your Obsidian vault through MCPVault, from any MCP client, with frontmatter preserved.

name: Obsidian Vault as the Core of Your Agent Harness
description: Use an Obsidian vault as the shared memory and control surface for your agents.

name: OKF: consume a bundle without blowing your context window
description: Use index.md for progressive disclosure so an agent navigates the graph instead of swallowing the whole folder, with reserved files that follow the spec.

name: OKF: generate a bundle from your schema, then ground it with citations
description: Mirror Google's reference pattern: a model drafts one OKF concept per table or module, and a stricter project rule requires a # Citations section on anything with a resource, so the knowledge is checkable, not just plausible.

name: OKF: turn your repo's tribal knowledge into a bundle your agent reads first
description: Write one markdown concept per thing worth knowing, cross-linked, as a conformant OKF bundle in version control that any agent can read with no SDK.

name: One AGENTS.md, no drift: prove CLAUDE.md is a real symlink and the generated files are in sync
description: Keep one AGENTS.md as the single source of agent rules, symlink CLAUDE.md to it, and prove with CI that the symlink is committed as a symlink (not a Windows-materialised copy) and that any generated per-tool file byte-matches a fresh regeneration from the source, so nothing silen

name: One shared memory for every coding agent: prove the configs actually point at the same server
description: Wire a Markdown memory MCP server (Basic Memory or an Obsidian MCP) into Claude Code, Cursor and Cline, and prove with CI that all three resolve to one server, that a write-the-memory house rule exists, and that the vault is under Git before any agent gets write access.

name: OpenCode: a model-routed team, cheap to plan, strong to build
description: Give each agent its own model so planning and review run on a cheap model and only the build runs on your best one.

name: OpenCode: a read-only Plan pass that cannot touch your files
description: Separate think from touch: lock the plan agent to read-only (edit + bash deny) so it proposes before it edits, then Tab into build to execute.

name: OpenCode: a reviewer subagent gated to exactly the Git commands you allow
description: Define a Markdown agent whose bash access is scoped per command (Git diff and grep yes, everything else no) and that can never write.

name: OpenCode: add an MCP tool, then lock it to one agent
description: Plug in an MCP server (live docs via Context7) but disable it globally and switch it on only for the one agent that needs it, so it does not burn tokens every turn.

name: OpenCode: run it headless in scripts and CI, with JSON output
description: Use opencode run non-interactively with --format json and a read-only agent so a pipeline gets machine-readable events and can never edit or execute.

name: OpenHands + Fable 5: Autonomous Issue to Pull Request
description: Hand Fable 5 a GitHub issue and let OpenHands plan, edit, run tests, and open a PR in a Docker sandbox.

name: OpenMontage: run a full AI video pipeline with zero paid APIs
description: Wire OpenMontage's scripting-to-composition pipeline using only free sources (Piper TTS for narration, Archive.org/NASA/Wikimedia for footage, Pexels for images) so you pay nothing for the orchestration layer, and validate the pipeline config before you run it.

name: OrcaRouter for coding: judge by passing tests, not by vibes
description: Fan a hard coding task out to a panel and keep the candidate whose patch actually passes your tests, using the tests_pass arbiter.

name: OrcaRouter: only fan out when it is worth it
description: Gate the expensive fan-out behind a difficulty condition so easy chat stays cheap and only hard requests pay for a panel.

name: Orch8: validate a bounded durable ReAct loop before model or tool calls
description: Pin and structurally validate Orch8's durable ReAct sequence before deployment, so an unbounded loop, broken route, embedded endpoint, credential field, or unresolved block reference fails in CI before any model or tool can run.

name: pgvector on Postgres you already run: prove you picked the right distance operator
description: Use pgvector in the Postgres you already run instead of standing up a dedicated vector database, and prove the distance operator you query with ( L2, cosine, or inner product) matches your embeddings, so your semantic search doesn't silently rank the wrong rows first.

name: Pi: The Reusable Prompt Template
description: Turn a prompt you retype into a permanent Pi slash command.

name: Pi: The Reusable Team Skill
description: Encode a multi-step task once as an Agent Skill your whole team installs.

name: Pi: The Safe Diff Reviewer
description: A code reviewer that reads your staged diff and structurally cannot modify it.

name: Pick a model with evidence: a GitHub Models bake-off that fits the free cap
description: Run the few prompts that actually matter across several models on GitHub Models' free tier, then keep the winner, with the daily call budget proven to fit before you start.

name: Postiz: Plan and Schedule a Week of Social Posts
description: From one brief, have an agent draft per-channel posts and queue a non-colliding weekly schedule in self-hosted Postiz.

name: promptfoo: make agent evals fail the build, not the user
description: Write a declarative promptfoo config with real assertions and wire promptfoo eval into CI, so a regression in prompt or agent behavior fails a check instead of reaching production.

name: Prove your meeting-notes pipeline never phones home (and gates on consent)
description: Run capture -> whisper.cpp transcription -> Ollama summary fully on your machine, with a CI check that every endpoint is loopback, no cloud host or API key appears anywhere in the config, and recording is gated on a consent acknowledgment.

name: QM: prove the destructive-action denials hold in every security posture, even the loosest
description: Run YC's company-wide QM agent with one org-wide security posture, and prove the predeclared hard denials (recursive delete, destructive SQL, mass delete) are refused in every posture including the loosest, so loosening the posture only relaxes approvals, never the destructive-ac

name: Read your token receipts right: volume and cost are different leaderboards
description: Attribute your model usage by both tokens and dollars, so you can see the flip the OpenRouter rankings show: cheap open models dominate volume while premium models dominate spend, and never mistake a high token ranking for value.

name: Rebuild Fable 5's deep-research fan-out on your own keys (OrcaRouter)
description: Fan a research prompt out to a panel of models you choose, then fuse or judge the answers with an arbiter, in a routing DSL you version and control.

name: ReMe pattern: define prospective memory as a schedule your agent can tick off
description: Write a reminder schedule config that an agent can load to surface its own future obligations — follow-ups, timed checks, recurring digests — and validate the structure before wiring it up.

name: Repomix + Fable 5: Pack a Repo for a Long-Context Review
description: Flatten an entire codebase into a single file and let Fable 5 hold all of it at once for a whole-system review.

name: Research Ingestion: File a Source Into Your Knowledge Base
description: Paste an article or transcript into your vault and have Claude summarize, link, and flag contradictions.

name: Route through a gateway with a tested open-weights fallback
description: Keep model access from being a single point of failure: route through an OpenAI-compatible gateway and pin a fallback that is open-weights and has actually been tested, so a pulled or deprecated model is a two-minute config change, not a lost week.

name: Run GLM-5.2 for the bulk, escalate the hard turns to Opus 4.8
description: Wire a cost-routing config that sends most work to cheap hosted GLM-5.2 and only the hardest turns to Opus 4.8, instead of paying Opus prices for everything.

name: Run GLM-5.2 fully local on a Mac Studio and drive it with Hermes
description: Serve GLM-5.2's 2-bit GGUF on a Mac Studio over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, point Hermes at it as a custom provider, and hand it long hands-off agentic jobs.

name: Sakana Fugu: A/B it on your own task before you migrate
description: Point an OpenAI-compatible client at the Fugu endpoint and compare it to a single strong model on one hard task you already know the answer to, instead of trusting a benchmark chart.

name: Scrape politely: honor robots.txt and a crawl delay (the part most skip)
description: Gate any scraper behind a robots.txt check and a crawl delay so you only fetch what a site allows, at a rate it allows, using nothing but the Python standard library.

name: Self-Healing Test Loop: an Agent that Fixes Until Green
description: Wrap a coding agent in a bounded loop that re-runs your tests and fixes the code until the suite passes or it runs out of attempts.

name: Self-host CodeWiki on private code: validate the config before you spend tokens
description: Configure the open-source FSoft CodeWiki to generate architecture-aware docs on your own machine (so private code never leaves it), and validate the provider and model config before a full, token-spending run.

name: Self-hosting the open-source stack? Prove your backup actually restores before you need it
description: Make the one self-hosting discipline that matters a machine check: back up your database, destroy the live copy, restore from the backup, and assert the restored data matches the original exactly, so you find a broken backup in CI instead of at 2am.

name: Serve GLM-5.1 yourself for long-horizon agentic coding (vLLM)
description: Stand up the MIT-licensed GLM-5.1 FP8 checkpoint as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for long agentic runs, validated serve config + endpoint.

name: Serve MiniMax M3 yourself for agentic coding (vLLM)
description: Stand up MiniMax M3 on an 8x H200 node as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and point any coding agent at it, validated serve flags + endpoint config.

name: Serve NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra yourself for high-throughput agents (vLLM)
description: Stand up the NVFP4 Nemotron 3 Ultra checkpoint as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for fast, long-running agent loops, validated serve flags + endpoint.

name: Shepherd: prove an agent task is retained and least-privilege before it runs
description: Declare an agent task's per-repo read/write grants and hold its output to one side (retained, not applied), then validate that nothing auto-applies and every write grant is explicit, before you run it.

name: SkillSpector: fail your CI build on a risky agent skill
description: Scan every skill you did not write with SkillSpector and gate CI on the result, so a malicious or vulnerable SKILL.md fails the build instead of running with your agent's permissions at runtime.

name: STEM source → reviewable LaTeX notes with a sandboxed compile gate
description: Turn user-selected STEM references into source-tagged LaTeX study material while keeping installs and compilation opt-in, preserving discrepancies, and independently proving that every pinned upstream template compiles in Tectonic's untrusted mode.

name: Swap to a cheap image model, but guard the cases it loses
description: Default image generation to a cheap model for general scenes, while proving the cases the premium model dominates (text in the frame, charts, precise layout) are still routed to it, so the swap saves money without quietly degrading the work that has words in it.

name: Teach OpenCode Go your weekly chore once, then run it in minutes
description: Capture a repeating chore as a reusable OpenCode command backed by the Go plan's models, so a two-hour weekly task becomes a five-minute run.

name: Text your own AI assistant on WhatsApp: Hermes wired to FreeLLMAPI
description: Point Hermes Agent at a FreeLLMAPI backend and connect it to WhatsApp, so a memory-keeping assistant runs 24/7 on a free always-on server and costs nothing per message, with the wiring validated before you link a number.

name: Track a tool's hype curve across any Substack (no API key)
description: Count how often a tool or model is mentioned in a Substack's posts over time, so you can see a hype curve rise and fade, using only the public archive.

name: Turn a Hand-Drawn UI into Working Code with tldraw
description: Sketch a screen on an infinite canvas and have a vision model return a live, working version of it.

name: Unsloth: write parametric memory in with a fine-tune config
description: Write a valid Unsloth fine-tune config that bakes stable, always-needed domain knowledge into a small model so the knowledge is native rather than carried in a prompt on every call.

name: Validate a WrenAI semantic model's references before an agent queries through it
description: Before letting an agent query through WrenAI's governed semantic layer (MDL), validate that every relationship and metric resolves to a model and column that actually exist, so a stale definition fails a check instead of quietly returning wrong-but-plausible numbers.

name: Validate an Apple Core AI export entry and skill plugin before you touch a Mac
description: Check a Core AI model registry entry and the agent-skill plugin manifest offline, so you know the export recipe is well-formed before spending an evening on macOS 27.

name: Verify an agent-skills plugin before you ship or install it
description: Check that a Claude Code / agentskills.io skills package is structurally valid, every SKILL.md has proper frontmatter and a name matching its folder, and the plugin marketplace manifest parses, so a broken skill never fails to load after you publish it.

name: Vet a SKILL.md before you install it
description: Treat an agent skill like the untrusted dependency it is: parse its SKILL.md, confirm the frontmatter is well-formed, and surface every executable script it bundles, since the research flagged script-bearing skills as the most dangerous, before you ever let your agent run it.

name: Vet the fine print a star count hides: real license and a gate on dual-use tools
description: Before you build on a starred repo, record its actual license (not an assumed permissive one) and whether it is dual-use, so a custom license or an impersonation risk never surprises you after you have shipped.

name: Voyager pattern: validate a procedural skill store before you trust a saved skill
description: Capture a working routine as a named, described skill entry and validate the skill-library structure, so saved skills are findable and reviewable before an agent reuses them.

name: WebMCP: declare a site's agent tools, and gate the ones that spend money
description: Publish a WebMCP tool manifest so an agent calls named site tools instead of guessing at buttons, and validate that every tool has a real schema and every sensitive tool (pay, checkout, delete) requires a human confirmation before it runs.

name: Weekly Review: a Finished Review Instead of a Blank Page
description: Every Friday, have Claude Code turn your week's note activity into a written review.

name: Wire GLM-5.2 into Hermes: valid route, 64k-context check, no key in config
description: Validate a Hermes Agent config that runs GLM-5.2 through a real provider route (direct Z.AI or OpenRouter), clears Hermes's 64k minimum context, and keeps the API key out of config.yaml, before you start a session.

name: Wire the DeepWiki MCP into your agent so it looks up repos instead of hallucinating
description: Give your coding agent the DeepWiki MCP server so it can pull real context about an unfamiliar dependency mid-task, and validate the client config declares the three documented tools before you trust it.

name: Write an agent loop in code with smolagents (sandboxed)
description: Stand up a smolagents CodeAgent that writes Python to act instead of emitting JSON tool calls, and run that model-written code in a sandbox, not on your machine.

name: zvec: run vector search inside your app, no server, offline
description: Embed a vector database directly into your process with zvec, insert vectors, and query for nearest neighbors, with no separate server to run, config, or babysit.
